languageModelTools.name: search_confluence
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the organization's Confluence knowledge base (internal wiki) for pages matching a free-text query. Use this to ground answers in company/institution-specific documentation, standards, runbooks, architecture decisions, onboarding guides, and policies that are not in the codebase. Returns a ranked list of matching pages, each with a title, numeric id, URL, and a short excerpt. To read a page's full content, follow up with get_confluence_page using the returned id. Requires the user to have configured a Confluence base URL, account email, and API token.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search your organization's Confluence wiki to answer questions using internal documentation.

query.description: Free-text search terms describing the information to find in Confluence (e.g. 'deployment runbook for payments service').

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to return (1-15). Defaults to 5.

languageModelTools.name: get_confluence_page
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch the full plain-text content of a single Confluence page by its numeric id (as returned by search_confluence). Use this after search_confluence to read the details of the most relevant page(s) before answering. The page body is HTML-stripped and may be truncated if very long. Requires the user to have configured Confluence access.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the full content of a specific Confluence page.

pageId.description: The numeric Confluence page id to fetch (obtained from search_confluence results).

languageModelTools.name: search_jira
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the organization's Jira issue tracker for issues/tickets matching a free-text query, most-recently-updated first. Use this to ground answers in tickets, bug reports, acceptance criteria, and work status that aren't in the codebase. Returns a list of issues, each with a key (e.g. PROJ-123), summary, type, status, assignee, and URL. To read an issue's full description, follow up with get_jira_issue using the returned key. Requires the user to have configured a Jira base URL plus Atlassian email and API token.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search your organization's Jira issues to answer questions using ticket data.

query.description: Free-text search terms describing the issue(s) to find (e.g. 'payment retry timeout bug').

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return (1-20). Defaults to 5.

languageModelTools.name: get_jira_issue
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch the full details of a single Jira issue by its key (e.g. PROJ-123, as returned by search_jira), including summary, type, status, priority, assignee, reporter, and the HTML-stripped description. Use this after search_jira to read a ticket's details before answering. Requires the user to have configured Jira access.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the full details of a specific Jira issue.

issueKey.description: The Jira issue key to fetch, like 'PROJ-123' (obtained from search_jira results).

languageModelTools.name: search_github
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search GitHub across the organization for issues/pull requests, code, or repositories beyond the currently-open workspace. Use this to ground answers in other repos, related tickets/PRs, or where a symbol or pattern is used org-wide. Set 'type' to 'issues' (default, includes PRs), 'code', or 'repositories'. Results are scoped to the configured GitHub org when usageLogger.githubOrg is set. Returns a list of results with a title, detail, and URL. Requires the user to have stored a GitHub personal access token (code search in particular requires authentication).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search your organization's GitHub issues, PRs, code, and repositories.

query.description: Search terms. May include GitHub search qualifiers (e.g. 'repo:owner/name', 'in:title', 'state:open').

type.description: What to search: 'issues' (issues and pull requests, default), 'code', or 'repositories'.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20). Defaults to 5.

usageLogger.enablePassiveCapture.description: Automatically watch and parse local Copilot Chat session files.

usageLogger.retentionDays.description: Delete logged requests older than this many days. 0 = keep forever.

usageLogger.enableCompanyWideReporting.description: Opt-in: periodically send an AGGREGATE-ONLY usage report (counts by category/language/model/day — never prompt or response text) to usageLogger.reportingEndpointUrl.

usageLogger.reportingEndpointUrl.description: Internal endpoint that receives aggregate-only usage reports. Must be https:// unless usageLogger.allowInsecureHttp is set.

usageLogger.reportingIntervalMinutes.description: How often to send the company-wide report, in minutes.

usageLogger.allowInsecureHttp.description: Allow usageLogger.reportingEndpointUrl to be plain http:// instead of https://. Only enable for a trusted, isolated intranet endpoint.

usageLogger.reportingTransport.description: Transport for company-wide reporting: an HTTPS endpoint, or a local/internal MongoDB collection.

usageLogger.mongoDatabase.description: MongoDB database name for company-wide reporting (used when usageLogger.reportingTransport is 'mongodb'). Connection string is set separately via 'Copilot Usage: Set MongoDB Connection String' (stored securely, not here).

usageLogger.mongoCollection.description: MongoDB collection name for company-wide reporting (used when usageLogger.reportingTransport is 'mongodb').

usageLogger.privateMode.description: Pause all Copilot usage logging (passive capture and the @usage participant still run, but nothing is written to the local database). Toggle via 'Copilot Usage: Toggle Private Mode'.

enumDescriptions: Show remaining cost-unit budget for today (requires usageLogger.monthlyCreditLimit; falls back to request count otherwise).
usageLogger.statusBarDisplay.description: What the status bar item's primary text shows.

usageLogger.excludedPathGlobs.description: Glob patterns (e.g. '**/secrets/**', '**/*.pem'). Any Copilot request that has an attached file matching one of these is skipped entirely — not even its metadata is logged.

usageLogger.sensitiveLabelKeywords.description: Keywords (e.g. 'CONFIDENTIAL', 'RESTRICTED') checked against prompt/response text and attached file paths. Matching requests still have metadata (category/language/model/timestamp) logged, but prompt and response text are redacted before being stored locally. NOTE: this is a local-storage control only — it cannot prevent data from being sent to the Copilot model itself. Use GitHub Copilot's org-level Content Exclusion policy for that.

usageLogger.monthlyCreditLimit.description: Optional monthly Copilot cost-unit budget to track against on the dashboard (based on the per-request 'copilotCredits' value VS Code reports — a relative cost signal, not guaranteed to exactly match GitHub's official premium-request billing meter). 0 = don't show a limit.

usageLogger.timeSavingsMinutesPerCategor.description: Override the default estimated-minutes-saved-per-request values (by category, e.g. {"debug-fix": 20}) used for the dashboard's 'Estimated time saved' card. This is always a rough heuristic estimate, never a measurement — leave empty to use the built-in defaults.

usageLogger.confluenceBaseUrl.description: Base URL of your Confluence Cloud wiki, including the /wiki suffix (e.g. https://yourcompany.atlassian.net/wiki). Enables the search_confluence and get_confluence_page chat tools. The API token is set separately via 'Copilot Usage: Set Confluence API Token' (stored securely, not here).

usageLogger.confluenceEmail.description: The Atlassian account email used with your Confluence API token for authentication.

usageLogger.atlassianEmail.description: Optional: Atlassian account email for Confluence AND Jira. If empty, usageLogger.confluenceEmail is used. The single Atlassian API token (set via 'Copilot Usage: Set Confluence API Token') authenticates both products.

usageLogger.jiraBaseUrl.description: Base URL of your Jira Cloud site, without a trailing path (e.g. https://yourcompany.atlassian.net). Enables the search_jira and get_jira_issue chat tools. Uses the same Atlassian email + API token as Confluence.

usageLogger.githubOrg.description: Optional GitHub organization/login to scope the search_github chat tool to (e.g. 'my-company'). Leave empty to search across everything the token can see.
